newsitem.title: UK: Smokers see pink and quit after urine test.
newsitem.headline: Smokers see pink and quit after urine test.

text.p: Pregnant British women cut down on their smoking or even quit after seeing the results of simple tests in which nicotine turned their urine pink -- and the more they smoked, the pinker it got.
The New Scientist weekly said on Thursday that a new test turned urine pink in the presence of nicotine and its breakdown products.
"Smokers tend to underestimate their consumption," researcher Graham Cope of the University of Birmingham in central England was quoted as saying in the study.
"They were more aware of their habit," he said after screening 1,000 pregnant women in a pilot study.
Cope, who developed the test, said 20 percent of cigarette-smoking patients shown the results of the quick tests quit while another 30 percent cut down significantly.
The test could also help would-be quitters to measure their progress and monitor the dangers faced by children from passive smoking, he said.
